outcome: Help store leaders align tasks and staffing to demand, service, replenishment and compliance while respecting labour rules and manager authority.
overview: Store managers build rosters and task lists by hand against traffic that moves with the weather, the football calendar and Ramadan trading hours, then absorb the overtime when a delivery lands late. This solution forecasts store demand by hour and department, generates roster and task plans inside hard labour, skills, break and safety constraints, and presents them to the manager to edit and approve — never to publish automatically. Employee signals stay aggregated; no individual performance scoring happens outside approved policy. An 8–12 week store-cluster pilot measures avoidable overtime, task completion, service and availability against a control group, with employee feedback reviewed throughout.

benefits.text: Reduce avoidable overtime or task delay by a target 10% on the pilot store cluster
benefits.source: Redington Retail catalogue; consistent with published workforce-management benchmark ranges
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target to validate against a control cluster during the pilot — not a guarantee, and it is bounded by contract and rota constraints the customer sets

benefits.text: Improve service and on-shelf availability by aligning replenishment tasks to demand rather than habit
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on task-data quality and delivery-schedule reliability; store execution remains a manager responsibility

benefits.text: Honour labour, skills, break and safety constraints as hard rules on every published plan
benefits.source: Reference design — constraints enforced before a plan reaches a manager, with manager approval mandatory
benefits.limits: A design property verified in constraint tests; correctness depends on the customer’s encoded contract and labour rules

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); workforce and store data remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: No digital record of contracts, working-time rules, skills and availability
notFor.why: Constraint-based scheduling is only as safe as the rules it is given; missing rules become silent breaches

notFor.situation: No employee consultation route or works-council equivalent where required
notFor.why: Scheduling changes affect people directly; the design assumes consultation, notice and an appeal route exist

notFor.situation: The intent is individual worker performance scoring or productivity surveillance
notFor.why: The reference design prohibits it — signals are aggregated and used to plan work, not to rank people

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns labour policy, employee consultation and every published schedule · Duration: 8–12 weeks pilot; further 16–26 weeks to enterprise scale
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, forecasting data scientist, optimisation engineer, integration engineer; customer store-operations owner, HR and employee-relations lead, health-and-safety reviewer, payroll owner, pilot store managers · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery, constraint capture and labour-cost baseline
2) Workforce and demand data integration
3) Forecast build and constraint-model configuration with HR sign-off
4) Manager workbench, colleague app and payroll reconciliation testing
5) Controlled store-cluster pilot against a matched control
6) Benefit review, employee-feedback review and handover
deliverables: Every encoded labour, skills, break and safety constraint demonstrated to block an infeasible plan
Planned, worked and paid hours reconcile with payroll on the pilot cluster
Service and safety measures held or improved against the control cluster
Manager and colleague UAT completed with notice and appeal routes exercised
Privacy and security reviews complete and the finance baseline confirmed
effort: 8–12 weeks pilot; further 16–26 weeks to enterprise scale
languages: English delivery; Arabic and English manager and colleague interfaces supported
